_metadata.independence: I read only the brief and the single input file x18-re-input.json; no other files, searches, web or APIs were used.

hints.reason: ARM via hugging with your arms, BEAR via the instantly familiar bear hug; clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Clean, easy pair. RIGHT (right arm / right to bear arms) is a cleverer alternative but brushes a political topic; HUG is the safer pick.

hints.reason: DONKEY via the name Donkey Kong, BANANA via the bananas he collects in the Donkey Kong Country games; a broadly known reference.

pairs.pair_note: Solid pop-culture pair; bananas are a series staple from Donkey Kong Country onward, not the original arcade game, which the text does not claim.

hints.reason: BASEBALL and CRICKET are both bat-and-ball sports; obvious but correct, with a small bonus that bat and cricket are also both animals.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, fair clue; lines are accurate.

hints.reason: Sasquatch is Bigfoot, so BIG and FOOT snap together as the two halves of its other name; a satisfying click.

pairs.pair_note: Nice aha: the hint is the synonym of the compound the two targets form.

hints.reason: Classic double meaning: a novel is a BOOK and novel means NEW.

pairs.pair_note: Textbook double meaning; strong.

hints.reason: BROOM via sweeping, CLEAN via the idiom clean sweep (and literal cleaning); fair and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Good easy clue; the sports sense of clean sweep adds a light second layer.

hints.reason: CAMERA via the Canon brand is solid, but CANNON is reached only as a one-letter-off sound-alike of the target, which nearly gives the target away and sits close to the contained-in-target rule; SHOOT (shoot a photo, shoot a cannon) is a true double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Homophone near-spelling of a target; would prefer SHOOT. Second opinion welcome on whether a sound-alike of a target should count as near-containment.

hints.reason: CAPTAIN via skipper as a synonym, PENGUIN via Skipper, leader of the Madagascar penguins; the synonym is earned by a real second link.

pairs.pair_note: Fun aha; Madagascar penguins are widely known.

hints.reason: LETTER via capital letter, CASE via upper case = capital letters and also capital case (a death-penalty case); two true routes to CASE.

pairs.pair_note: The uppercase route is the one most players will see; the legal sense is a true bonus.

hints.reason: SNOW via snowflakes, CEREAL via corn flakes and Frosted Flakes; clear and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, pleasant clue.

hints.reason: CHESS via the white pieces, FIRST via the well-known rule that white moves first; indirect but it clicks once you think of chess.

pairs.pair_note: OPENING (a chess opening; opening = first) is a double-meaning alternative that could also pass; WHITE is the more aha-style fact link.

hints.reason: CLOCK via telling the hour is fine, but SHORT is reached only through the hour hand being the short hand; HAND (clock hand, shorthand) is a clearly stronger double meaning and HOUR is unremarkable beside it.

pairs.pair_note: Swap to HAND: clock hand + shorthand is a real 10/10 candidate.

hints.reason: COCKTAIL via gin as a spirit, COTTON via the cotton gin machine; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong double meaning with accurate lines.

hints.reason: A Crock-Pot is a slow cooker, so SLOW and COOK combine into the thing the hint names; clear and familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Brand is normally written Crock-Pot; the closed-up CROCKPOT is a common informal spelling and reads fine.

hints.reason: CROSS via crossing your fingers, LUCK via the gesture's meaning of wishing for luck; one instantly familiar custom joins both.

pairs.pair_note: Easy and fair.

hints.reason: SLIDE completes Electric Slide and DANCE is what the Electric Slide is; an instantly familiar party-dance name.

pairs.pair_note: Phrase-join but the phrase is iconic and the category side makes it click.

hints.reason: One idiom carries both: rearranging the DECK chairs on the TITANIC; satisfying for adults who know the saying, and deck chairs alone gets DECK.

pairs.pair_note: Idiom is well known to U.S. adults, less so to younger players; SHIP would be safer but flat.

hints.reason: DINOSAUR as the category, PLATE via the stegosaurus's famous back plates; category plus property, like PENGUIN for Antarctica.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate and fair.

hints.reason: QUIET calls up 'you could hear a PIN DROP', which holds both targets in one idiom; indirect with a nice payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect idiom clue; SILENCE would work similarly.

hints.reason: EGYPT via Giza and MEXICO via Teotihuacan and Chichen Itza; both are famous for ancient pyramids.

pairs.pair_note: Mexico side is a mild aha for players who default to Egypt only.

hints.reason: FACE via poker face, FIRE via the fireplace poker; a clean double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: FATHER via 'I am your father' and MASK via Vader's iconic black mask; two of the most famous facts about him.

pairs.pair_note: Excellent pop-culture clue.

hints.reason: FIRST via the first U.S. president, QUARTER via his profile on the coin; indirect familiar knowledge with a real click.

pairs.pair_note: RELATIVE-style indirect aha; strong.

hints.reason: THUMB via green thumb, GARDEN via what a green thumb is good at (and green as the garden's color); instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Easy, satisfying idiom clue.

hints.reason: METAL via iron the element, GOLF via irons the clubs; same shape as the owner's DRIVER favourite.

pairs.pair_note: Clear double meaning.

hints.reason: POLICE via the police badge is instant; GYM rests on Pokemon gym badges, a core and hugely popular mechanic but one that older or non-gaming players may not link.

pairs.pair_note: Judgement call: Pokemon gym badges are mainstream pop culture, not niche fandom, so PASS, but it could reasonably be BORDERLINE for an older audience. No obviously better hint found.

hints.reason: HEAD and TAIL via heads or tails on a coin flip; obvious but correct and fair.
hints.fix: HEAD line: Heads is one side of a coin.

pairs.pair_note: Very easy; the HEAD line's 'the other side' reads oddly when shown on its own.

hints.reason: HIGH via soprano as the highest standard voice, OPERA via sopranos singing leading opera roles; accurate and fair.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: ICE via ice cube, PUZZLE via Rubik's Cube; a neat pairing.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: JUNGLE via where Tarzan lives, SWING via his vine-swinging; both are signature traits.

pairs.pair_note: Classic, fair.

hints.reason: KNIGHT via medieval times, MIDDLE via the Middle Ages that medieval names; a satisfying indirect click.

pairs.pair_note: Good aha; MIDDLE is the side players have to work for.

hints.reason: RED via scarlet as a shade, LETTER via The Scarlet Letter; a familiar classic that clicks.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: MOON via the Apollo 11 walk, MAN via 'first man on the Moon' and 'one small step for man'; clear and accurate.

pairs.pair_note: Fair; note ARMSTRONG contains ARM, which matters only if ARM shares a board with this pair.

hints.reason: TURTLE via the Ninja Turtles, MASK via their signature colored eye masks; broadly known.

pairs.pair_note: Good; colored masks are the famous cartoon version, which is what most players know.

hints.reason: MOUTH via mouthwash, SOAP via washing, and the old threat 'wash your mouth out with soap' ties both targets into one phrase.

pairs.pair_note: Nice that a single familiar saying holds both targets.

hints.reason: NOTE via the octave running from a note to its namesake, SCALE via a major scale filling an octave; correct music link, if plain.

pairs.pair_note: Accurate but low-delight; a double-meaning hint using SCALE's fish or weight sense would be more fun if one exists.

hints.reason: SUIT via a tuxedo being a formal suit, PENGUIN via its tuxedo-like coloring (a tux is even called a penguin suit); clicks instantly.

pairs.pair_note: Strong; the text stays metaphorical, which is correct.

hints.reason: TEAM via the name Team Rocket, POKEMON via the villains of the Pokemon anime; the name is iconic enough to click.

pairs.pair_note: Name-contains-target phrase-join, but Team Rocket is one of the best-known parts of Pokemon.

hints.reason: MOSS calls up 'a rolling stone gathers no moss', which carries both ROLL and STONE; indirect with a good payoff.

pairs.pair_note: Good indirect proverb clue; the STONE line's 'says the proverb' is an implication rather than the wording, but acceptable.

hints.reason: One idiom holds both: draw the SHORT STRAW; instantly familiar.

pairs.pair_note: Easy idiom clue; fine.

hints.reason: SNOW via Elsa's snow and ice powers, SISTER via her sister Anna; Frozen is near-universal.

pairs.pair_note: Solid.

hints.reason: SPY via James Bond, STOCK via stocks and bonds; a crisp double meaning.

pairs.pair_note: Strong.

hints.reason: VEGETABLE via Popeye's spinach, STRONG via the strength it gives him; a classic cartoon link.

pairs.pair_note: Older but widely known; fine.
